Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the rear-end collision in
Pearland, Texas. Can you tell me where you were seated at the time?
A: I was in the front psasenger seat of my friend's car. We were stopped at a red light on the access road when it
happened.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the impact?
A: Not really. I was looking down at my phone, and the first thing I remember is a loud bang and my whole body
jerking forward and then back.
Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?
A: Yes, I was. The belt locked up hard when we were hit.
Q: Did you hit anything inside the car?
A: My right shoulder went into the door frame and my head snapped sideways. I didn't hit the windshield.
Q: Did you get out of the vehicle or seek medical care afterward?
A: The paramedics came and checked me out at the scene. They wanted me to go to the hospital, but I said I'd be
fine. The next morning my shoulder was really stiff and it hurt to lift my arm, so I went to my family doctor.
Q: What treatment have you received since then?
A: The doctor ordered an X-ray and an MRI. I've been going to physical therapy twice a week. I still can't reach
overhead without pain, and I'm having trouble sleeping on that side.
Q: Have you missed any work because of your shoulder?
A: I missed about four days. I work a desk job, so I've been able to do some of it from home since then.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I want to get better and I'm doing everything my doctor tells me. Thank you for listening.
</page>
